You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

A good starting point for TV series popularity analysis is to compare series by average viewers, rating, audience share, and weekly rank.

```sql
SELECT
    c.series_name,
    c.Country,
    c.Language,
    COUNT(ts.id) AS episode_count,
    AVG(CAST(ts.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
    AVG(CAST(ts.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
    AVG(ts.Share) AS avg_share,
    MIN(ts.Weekly_Rank) AS best_weekly_rank
FROM TV_series ts
JOIN TV_Channel c
    ON ts.Channel = c.id
GROUP BY
    c.series_name,
    c.Country,
    c.Language
ORDER BY
    avg_viewers_m DESC,
    avg_rating DESC,
    avg_share DESC;
```
I also wanna find out the min share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT
    MIN(Share) AS min_share
FROM TV_series;
```
I also wanna find the max share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT
    MAX(Share) AS max_share
FROM TV_series;
```
